headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; Plandex reads/writes the project directory and uses stdin/stdout. Their shared local-filesystem bridge makes instruction-like content from one agent plausibly consumed by the other in default coding workflows, though not as directly as a shared MCP server.
conditions: IF the same workspace directory is opened in both agents, injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent parses file contents or plan text as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require manual review of any text copied from one agent to the other.
Use read-only mounts for shared reference files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to inter-agent file handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and can egress broadly to model providers/MCP servers; Plandex also reads project files and sends context to its model provider or server. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent into the other and onward to third parties in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, file contents can be exposed to both backends.
IF clipboard contents include secrets, Cursor can ingest them and Plandex may later read them from files or pasted text.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Use separate API keys and accounts for each agent.
Clear clipboard before switching agents.
Restrict both agents to non-sensitive repos.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, modify git state, read/write the same filesystem, and run subprocesses. Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, while Plandex shares state via its server backend and stages changes before apply. Concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt git or files without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, simultaneous writes can conflict.
IF one agent auto-runs commands while the other stages/apply changes, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign one agent per repository at a time.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or stash after each agent's turn.
Avoid auto-apply/Yolo modes during overlap.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks across agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor runs a multi-step agent loop and can use MCP/tools; Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply. If Plandex consumes Cursor-produced code or plans as authoritative, or Cursor acts on Plandex output without verification, mistakes can cascade into executed shell commands or committed bad changes.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Cursor output as the source of truth, unverified errors can propagate into apply steps.
IF Cursor follows Plandex-generated instructions into shell or git actions, downstream mistakes become persistent.
mitigations: Require human review before apply/commit.
Cross-check outputs against source files.
Disable auto-apply and Yolo modes.
Use small, isolated tasks per agent.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state conflicting residency, certification, or retention terms. Cursor handles clipboard contents and model-provider traffic, while Plandex handles project files and model-provider/server traffic, but no explicit compliance mismatch is documented here, so only a low, documentation-gap risk is supportable.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data through either agent, external processing terms must be checked separately.
IF one deployment has stricter retention than the other, the mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared projects.
Review vendor privacy terms before use.
Use self-hosted or local-only deployments where available.
Separate datasets by compliance class.
requires-engineering: document and enforce retention/residency policy alignment.
